results.name: disposable PostgreSQL 16 migrated through the journal (incl. 0007) and the API is healthy behind the proxy with no provider configured
two synthetic invoices saved by the operator
one invoice has a SIMULATED 'created' operation row, the other has none
operator signs in through the browser and lands on the dashboard
on the dashboard, Check invoice status opens the status selector inside Nudgey (the panel stays open and the page did not change)
the search box has focus and the initial load is one bounded POST (limit 20, no term) to the existing search route
both saved invoices are listed with their own currency and total, and the SIMULATED draft row shows as 'PayPal draft created' while the other shows 'No PayPal draft'
the draft-only disclaimer is shown and nothing claims paid, unpaid, overdue or settled
typing a customer name sends ONE debounced POST whose body carries q; no URL contains the name
selecting an invoice shows its customer, amount and draft state, with Open invoice details
a search with no match says so plainly and clears the selection
when the server cannot be reached the selector shows an honest offline error with Try again, never an empty-account message
Try again repeats the same search and shows the matching invoice
Open invoice details opens the existing saved-invoice page for that invoice and closes Nudgey
View my invoices still navigates straight to the dashboard and closes the panel
Back returns to the Nudgey home actions
reopening the selector starts clean: nothing is selected and the search box is empty
at 390px the selector panel is inside the viewport, above the mobile navigation, with no horizontal overflow
Escape closes Nudgey and focus returns to the launcher
signing out removes the workspace, the selector and every invoice name from the page
only auth, invoice search (POST), the invoice detail read, its follow-up read and the follow-up list were used: never parse, PayPal-draft, a follow-up write or a send
no request left the page origin and no URL carries customer text
the only PayPal row is the SIMULATED one inserted for the label test; nothing was created, no approvals or webhooks, no follow-up written
browser storage is empty and the only console errors are the pre-sign-in 401 probe and the deliberately blocked search
